texts.preamble: Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Kabc020133162020 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch_25) -: Present:- Smt. Prakriti Kalyanpur, B.A(L),Ll.B., Ll.M. Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru. Dated This The 2nd Day Of January 2024 Mvc No.2854/2020 And 2855/2020 Petitoner/S: 1. Smt. Malini G.S. In Mvc:2854/2020: W/o Late g.S.Phanibabu Aged about 43 years, 2. Mr. Vikas Ghati S/o Late G.S.Phanibabu, Aged about 20 years, 3.
texts.facts: 3. It is the further case of the Petitioners (in MVC No.2854/2020) that, immediately G.S.Phanibabu was shifted to Vijayashree hospital, Bangalore and death was confirmed in the hospital. Post mortem was done on 25.07.2020 at KIMS Hospital & Research Centre and dead body was handed over to his family. Prior to the accident, deceased G.S.Phanibabu was working as a National Sales & Business Development manager (Food) at ALS Testing 6 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 Services India Private Limited, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.14,36,255/ per annum. He was also working as a Chief Advisor at Trans Tools Corporation, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.12,24,000/ per annum. So far, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards conveyance, transportation, obsequies and other religious ceremonies. 4. It is the further case of the Petitioner (in MVC No.2855/2020) that, immediately he was shifted Astar Super Specialty hospital, Bangalore, admitted as an inpatient, treated from 23.07.2020 to 25.07.2020 for the 7 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 injuries and discharged with advice. So far he has spent Rs.80,000/ towards treatment, medicines, nourishment and conveyance etc., At the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Project Manager at ALS Testing Services India Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.95,000/ per month. SCCH - 25 Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel but did not chose to file written statement. 7. Objection of the Respondent No.1. The respondent No.1/Insurance Company admitted issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and stated that it is valid from 31.10.2019 to 30.10.2020. This respondent denied the alleged accident, manner of accident and contended that insured vehicle is falsely implicated. Further the respondent No.1 has willfully handed over the possession of the vehicle to such person/rider who was not having valid and effective DL as on the date of accident. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. The present claim petitions are bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties. Further the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself. Further the Respondent No.1 denied the age, income, occupation of the petitioners and stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly 9 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 exorbitant. The Petitioners in both the cases in order to substantiate that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590, have got examined petitioner No.1 in MVC No.2854/2020 as PW.1 and Petitioner himself in MVC No.2855/2020 as PW.2 and produced 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9. Pws.1 & 2 have reiterated the averments of the petition in their affidavits filed in lieu of their chief examination. The Respondent No.1 on the other side has denied that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider. In the cross examination of PW.1, she has admitted that there are no street lights in Nice Road. In the cross examination of Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 10 PW.2, he has admitted that as per Ex.P.4 the Car was parked at nonparking area and where the pedestrian were 15 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 also not permitted to walk. He has further admitted that the traffic is heavy on that road. In support of the defence, the Respondent No.1 has examined its legal officer as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & R.2 authorization letter and copy of policy. The RW.1 has deposed in support of the defence of the respondent No.1. In the cross examination of RW.1 it is elicited that the respondent No.2 had DL to drive Two wheeler as on the date of accident. Therefore, from the crossexamination of Pws.1 and 2 and evidence of RW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the alleged manner of accident and hence the defence of the respondent No.1 that there was negligence on the part of the deceased is not acceptable. 13. Further, the FIR, FIS, spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA report, Inquest Mahazar, PM report, charge sheet and death certificate produced by the Petitioners as per Exs.P.1 to P.9 are public documents which are issued 16 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 by a public office and they have got presumptive value under law. She has also admitted that she received Rs.45,000/ twice for obsequies from the company. She has also admitted about receipt of Rs.10,00,000/ from the company. During the 30 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 crossexamination of PW.3 she has stated that Rs.10,00,000/ was given from insurance to the family of the deceased. Out of this, he was spending 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the petitioner has relied on (1) 2009 (II) ACC 444 Supreme Court of India: Bimladevi & Ors. And (3). 2021 ACJ 17 Supreme Court of India: Anita Sharma & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr., wherein the courts have held that the claimants have to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability. Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PWs.1 and 2 coupled with documents produced by them this court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 has ridden the same in a rash and 17 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 negligent manner, endangering human life, came with high speed and dashed against the deceased G.S.Phanibabu and the petitioner Raghavendra Rao P. and caused the accident, as a result of which both have sustained grievous injuries, due to which G.S.Phanibabu succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital. It is the further case of the Petitioner - Raghavendra Rao P. that as per wound certificate at Ex.P.16, on account of the accident, he has sustained (1) Concussive head injury, abrasion over right eyebrow, (2) Abrasion over left hand, (3) Blunt injury to chest. Tenderness + and (4) Contusion over forehead which are simple in nature. The Petitioner averred that due to these injuries, he suffered from disabilities, cannot walk for any long distance, suffering from severe headache and giddiness, suffering from partial loss of memory problems, cannot sleep sound and normal sleep, frequently suffering from illhealth problem, not able to do his daily routine work and often getting pain in his entire head region, cannot do any 20 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 manual hard work. The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field. He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability. Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and Raghavendra Rao. Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner is entitled to loss of Earned Leave. In support of the same, he has relied on (1) 2017 ACJ 1149 High Court of Delhi: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. R.K.Arora & Ors. And (2) 2021 21 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 ACJ 1691 High Court of Kerala: George Vs. Krishna Venu & Ors. wherein it is held that the injured is entitled to Loss of Leave with pay availed due to the disability or injury. According to Ex.P.21 the petitioner has availed 17 days Sick Leave. His Gross salary is Rs.1,07,520/. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to Rs.60,928/ for Loss of 17 days sick leave under the head Loss of income during laidup period. In addition, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.16 discloses that, he has sustained simple injuries. Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering. The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.80,000/ towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc., In this regard he has not produced any medical bills. Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled to any amount under the head of medical expenses. The Petitioners have further averred that due to the untimely death of deceased - G.S.Phanibabu, the Petitioners are suffering from mental pain and agony as they have lost their loving and affectionate family member. They have also pleaded that they are suffering from financial difficulties. 2019 ACJ 115 High Court of Delhi: SBI General Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Geetu and Ors. The petitioner counsel has also relied on this decision. 23. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Ins. Co. Ltd. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., & Ors., wherein it is held that if satisfactory evidence is available, higher percentage of addition for future prospects is permissible. But in the present case, PW.3 who came on behalf of employer of the deceased has admitted that the deceased was working as a permanent employee in their company. Moreover in the IT industry there is nothing called as a permanent job , employees keep changing their companies for better remuneration. The employee may quit or may be removed after due notice by the company. Therefore it can be safely assumed that the deceased was not a permanent employee and as per Pranay Sethi Case an addition of 25% to his income as future prospects should be made since the deceased is less than 50 years old. As per Sarla Verma's case, when there are two to three Dependants, 1/3rd of his monthly income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses. If 1/3 rd is deducted from the said amount it comes to Rs.13,50,596/. Therefore, the Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian iii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM: In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium. The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family. With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse". Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 24 24. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780. 35 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020 SCCH - 25 25. The Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 43 years and she has to live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ under the head of loss of consortium. Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the sons of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father. Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.40,000/ each, in total Rs.1,20,000/ is entitled under the head of loss of consortium. iv) LOSS OF ESTATE: Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate. As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled for a Raghavendra Rao.P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/ 25 sum of Rs.1,77,17,748/. If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,77,17,800/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum. LIABILITY 26. The Respondent No.1 has contended that the Two wheeler rider did not have a valid and effective DL. But has not led any evidence and hence it is clear that the respondents have failed to prove their defence. The Respondent No.1 has also taken the defence that there was negligence on the part of the deceased in parking the vehicle in National Highway. During the cross examination of PW.2 he has admitted that vehicles are not to be parked in Nice Road. However, the case of the petitioners is that they stopped their car due to tyre puncture.
